rationale: B wins slightly because it opens more real doors without padding: "The hard part of a circular sneaker is the mail: On scales a nationwide take-back loop" is a supply-chain story A simply leaves on the floor. A's best angle, "On's recycled-shoe pledge meets the question it won't answer: how much actually gets remade?", is sharper and cleaner than anything in B, but the overall set stays in the obvious subscription/sustainability/margins triangle. B has one bad habit - decorating facts with "operational graveyard" language - but it gives the founder more journalist-shaped routes to test.
gaps_in_A: Misses a supply-chain/reverse-logistics angle even though the update gives it the raw material: "then mail it back to be ground down and remade." That is not just sustainability; it is operations.
"putting a core product behind" overclaims. The update says Cyclon running shoe, not that Cyclon is a core product for On.
"Next step: `meanest-editor` ... draft a tight pitch" is the wrong handoff for an angle set; first move is source/proof collection or journalist-fit-check, not a roast tool.
It gestures at material distinctness in "the other angles drop to the material" but never actually gives the castor-bean/materials trade angle.
gaps_in_B: "take-back programs are widely seen as the operational graveyard of circular retail" is unsupported beat lore. Useful hunch, not a supplied fact.
"commercial-scale test for castor-bean materials" and "moving from pilot volume to nationwide distribution" stretch the update; nationwide subscription is disclosed, actual volume is not.
It buries the cleanest skeptical story in proof/questions instead of making it an angle: the undisclosed recycling rate.
"four viable shapes exist" is a little cocky when the materials and logistics angles both need basic technical details before they can survive a reporter call.
